video_title: How Much Cap Space Can The Lakers Realistically Create This Offseason?

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers' projected cap space after current contracts and cap holds
quotes.excerpt: The Lakers, if they only have the guys on the books that they're projected to have, they'd have about $49.2 million to play with.
quotes.quote: So you add in the eight players officially under contract, you add in the cap holds of Austin Reaves and Jackson Hayes, and then you add the two empty roster charges, and the Lakers get to $115,774,640. Now, the projected cap actually dropped back in March from projected to be $166 million to $165 million, so the cap is coming in a little bit lower. So if you look at the math there of $165 million for the cap, and we don't know the official number yet, but it's going to be in that ballpark, minus $115.7 million, that gets you to $49,225,360. So the Lakers, if they only have the guys on the books that they're projected to have, plus the number 25 pick, plus they keep the cap holds of Austin and Jackson, and then they have the two empty roster charges, they'd have about $49.2 million to play with.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Impact of key free agent cap holds on Lakers' salary
quotes.excerpt: LeBron's cap hold, for example, is $59.5 million. So as long as the Lakers have not rescinded the rights to LeBron, he will be on the books for $59.5 million.
quotes.quote: Now, let's look at the cap holds here because the cap holds are where things get a little tricky. LeBron's cap hold, for example, is $59.5 million. So as long as the Lakers have not rescinded the rights to LeBron, he will be on the books for $59.5 million. Rui is at $27.4 million. Austin as aforementioned is at $20.9 million. Luke is at $13.2 million. Jackson's at $4.5 million, and then Marcus is at $6.2 million if he opts out. He has a player option. I think he will opt out. I would be shocked if Marcus does not make double-digit millions next season. So if you take the LeBron, Rui, Luke, and Marcus cap holds, and we're putting Austin and Jackson to the side because they're already on the cap sheet, you add up those four players and their cap holds, you get $106.3 million.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers' salary projection with key player cap holds and potential reductions
quotes.excerpt: You're at $219 million, which means you are $3 million under the second apron.
quotes.quote: If you add that to LA's salary projection at this point, like you would take away $2.7 million from the empty roster charges, which would bring them down to $113 million, and then you add in those cap holds of $106 million, you're at $219 million, which means you are $3 million under the second apron. And so at that point, you would have 14 players under contract, you'd be about $3 million under the second apron, and LA could maybe sign a minimum player depending on their terms of service, otherwise they just would be standing pat with 14 players. Now, just because they're at the $219 million doesn't mean they're going to stay at the $219 million because I'd be shocked if LeBron is making $59.5 million from the Lakers next season. I would be shocked if Rui is making $27.4 million. So those two alone, if we knock down Rui to a range of $16 million to $20 million, maybe let's say $16 million to $18 million, and then LeBron is I've stated why I think LeBron is going to have to take a lot less or at least for what the Lakers' ambitions are this offseason, but let's just say the middle ground here is like $40 million for LeBron.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers face tough choices retaining LeBron, Rui, and Marcus Smart
quotes.excerpt: You are right there basically using all of your cap space on LeBron and Rui.
quotes.quote: If you have LeBron at $40 million, Rui at $18 million, even if you rescind the rights to Luke, and Marcus it's tricky because Marcus, the starting salary for Marcus is $6.2 million. That cap hold would be the most the Lakers can offer him without using cap space or an exception. So Marcus is not, he's not going to opt out of his current contract to then re-sign at $6.1 million, it would have to be more than that. So I think Marcus is going to be a guy they have to use either cap space or an exception on. But just with LeBron and Rui, even if you get rid of Luke, just LeBron and Rui, for argument's sake, that's $58 million, but even if you knock LeBron to $30 million, that's still $48 million, which I mentioned the cap number right now at $49.3 million. You are right there basically using all of your cap space on LeBron and Rui. That's to say nothing of Marcus who in this instance, you can't even use cap space on Marcus, you'd have to use the room exception, which is about $9.3 million, and that might be low for Marcus in my opinion, and you'd be losing Luke.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers' two paths: run it back or create cap space with sacrifices
quotes.excerpt: The Lakers kind of have like two paths here where they can run it back to a degree or they could be a cap space team.
quotes.quote: And so you run out of optionality pretty quickly. So the Lakers kind of have like two paths here where they can run it back to a degree with LeBron and Rui and Luke and Marcus or three of those four, and then use the non-taxpayer MLE and minimums to fill out the rest of the roster. Or they could be a cap space team, but to be a cap space team, LeBron either has to take a massive discount or leave, or they have to, he still probably has to take some sort of discount if they keep him. But then you're also losing Luke at a minimum and potentially Rui or Marcus depending on where their numbers come in. And honestly, if Rui's commanding $18 million to $20 million compared to Marcus at $10 million to $12 million, I already have been on the side of I would prefer to keep Marcus over Rui, and I think the Lakers should prioritize him more and will. But if it's like Marcus at $10 million versus Rui at $18 million, I think that's a no-brainer of I'd rather have the extra $8 million in flexibility to potentially add another above minimum contract or maybe that keeps Luke, right?

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers' tough choices: keeping Rui or Marcus, or pursuing restricted free agents
quotes.excerpt: It does feel like Rui or Marcus is going to become a choice at some point, and it's going to be difficult to keep both those guys.
quotes.quote: Would you rather have Marcus and Luke? Marcus for $10 million, Luke for $8 million, and you know, that's $18 million versus Rui at $18 million. I would rather have Marcus and Luke. So the Lakers are going to have some tough decisions here. I do see the more I look at their cap situation, it does feel like Rui or Marcus is going to become a choice at some point, and it's going to be difficult to keep both those guys. Now, the giant caveat here is if LeBron retires or if LeBron leaves, then they have a lot more space to play with. And again, if you go back to that $49.2 million, you could re-sign Rui at $18 million, Marcus at $12 million, that's $30 million, and you still have another $19.2 million to play with. But we haven't even talked about, like we're just dipping our toes in the water here. We haven't even talked about restricted free agency and if you make an offer for Walker Kessler because again, if you go Kessler, Payton Watson, Jalen Duren, Tari Eason, that's taking a decent chunk out of that $49 million.

quotes.speaker: Jovan Buha
quotes.summary_phrase: Lakers must shed salary and lose key players for flexibility
quotes.excerpt: It's really going to be like some combination of probably losing some of these key guys plus shedding salary to really get the flexibility.
quotes.quote: The Lakers are just going to have a ton of tough decisions to make, and that's why again when we talk about LeBron, I think that number's probably going to have to be in that $20 million to $25 million. If it's any higher, at some point it just it's really difficult to add to the roster even if you are shedding salary on top of that. Then they're going to have to decide how they feel about Rui, Marcus, and Luke, and what are the numbers they would want those guys back at, how many of those guys do they want back? And then depending on where they're at, they could have some cap space or they could be above the cap. And I will touch on this in more depth and go through each specific scenario in the coming days and weeks, but I wanted to give you a bit of an overview where yeah, you I mean you just quickly run out of money here as the Lakers. And it's really going to be like some combination of probably losing some of these key guys plus shedding salary to really get the flexibility. The Lakers are going to have to get creative and be very intentional with how they approach all this.
